correctness.rationale: A complete wordwise diameter-two anticode classification is proved, then the exact distance-two geodesics show precisely which plane/ball/tetra subsets are visible. Different maximal carriers are disjoint at extremal cardinalities; this validates the optimizer count, including the sole q=2 tetrahedral exception. The q≤6 matrix values have independent convex row-pair upper bounds and explicit C4-free lower constructions; the circulant modular-difference argument proves the q≥7 threshold in all orders. Direct finite exhaustive checks independently test the classification on six small boxes, but the infinite claim is established by proof, not extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The new claim is an all-parameter three-factor, nonbinary two-distance structural converse and a sharp extremal transition. The 2024 primary source provides the parameter and an isometric-subgraph lower bound, while the 2021 source solves the two-factor visibility-to-C4-free correspondence only. The 2023 Hamming paper concerns total visibility. The binary Hamming special case is acknowledged as covered. Neither a covering three-factor upper bound nor the transition follows as a stated corollary of these sources; checked full relevant sections and prior-result descriptions. Residual priority risks remain.
residual_risks: Unindexed or inaccessible later work on three-factor nonbinary k-distance mutual visibility or diameter-two Hamming anticodes might give an equivalent or stronger result.

The classical C4-free matrix extremal number and its exact multiplicity remain unsolved in general; the new claim is a structural reduction and a sharp cutoff, not a formula eliminating these quantities.
The 2026 publicly indexed binary-hypercube result overlaps the q=2 boundary, which is excluded from novelty and included for theorem completeness.

value.rationale: This determines a natural, previously unresolved selected-pair distance-limited invariant throughout all three-factor complete graph Cartesian products, with all maximum-set mechanisms and their multiplicities. The equality at q=6 and strict Zarankiewicz-dominated regime q≥7 reveal a sharp structural transition and transfer the large-alphabet optimum exactly to an established hard extremal matrix problem. It is more informative than a routine small-case computation or a restatement of the two-factor result; full numerical evaluation of Z is not asserted.
